title: The 8 Levels of Job Hunting
house: A bustling metropolis of produce people where towering glass office skyscrapers cast long shadows over cramped subway stations, neon-lit convenience stores, and damp apartment hallways.
catchphrase: The number on your forehead never lies.

levels.name: Oliver, 24, Fresh Graduate
levels.story: The 8 levels of job hunting after a master degree. Level 1. Level 1: 0 dollars in your bank account, 214 job rejections, and no way to pay rent. I stared at my glowing forehead display inside the cramped, damp studio kitchen while the notification pinged again. Another automated rejection email from yet another entry-level marketing firm. You have exactly twelve hours to clear out your stuff, kid, because your forehead shows you are completely worthless. I swallowed the lump in my throat and gripped the edge of the counter until my knuckles turned white. I have a Master degree in economics from state university, and you are treating me like street trash. Your little paper degree is worth less than toilet paper around here, loser. My chest tightened into a hard, painful knot as I looked down at the tiny gold coin hidden behind the sugar bowl. You will never amount to anything in this city. You will see that in Level 2. You'll see that in Level 2.

levels.name: Maya, 26, Unpaid Intern
levels.story: The 8 levels of job hunting after a master degree. Level 2. Level 2: 450 dollars stipend a month, working eighty hours a week, and still eating dry toast for dinner. I stood behind the sticky counter of the downtown coffee shop, wiping up spilled espresso while my forehead flashed my pathetic monthly survival money. The bell above the door chimed, and a sharp, citrus-scented lemon executive from the upper floors slapped a stack of unpaid invoices onto my tray. You call yourself an intern with a Master in finance, but you cannot even pour a proper latte without messing up the foam. My eyes burned with hot, stinging tears as I looked down at the tiny gold coin wedged inside the tip jar. I stayed up until three in the morning editing your quarterly tax reports for free, and you treat me like dirt. Your kind only belongs behind the counter, not in the boardroom. My stomach twisted into knots as the digital display on my forehead flickered nervously. Consider yourself permanently disqualified from the hiring pool. You will see that in Level 3. You'll see that in Level 3.

levels.name: Leo, 28, Freelance Copywriter
levels.story: The 8 levels of job hunting after a master degree. Level 3. Level 3: 1.850 dollars a month from random gigs, and my landlord is threatening to lock my door. I paced across the creaking wooden floor of my shared apartment, staring at my forehead display while my phone buzzed with another client cancellation. The front door swung open, and the sleek dragon fruit consultant from upstairs dropped an eviction notice onto my desk with a loud thud. With a Master in literature, you should be making real money instead of writing cheap blog posts for five bucks. My jaw clenched so hard I tasted metallic iron as I spotted a tiny gold coin gleaming underneath the radiator. I worked seventy hours last week on your campaign, and you have not paid me a single dime. Amateurs like you clog up the system for the rest of us professionals. My heart hammered wildly against my ribs as cold sweat broke out across my shell. Your contract is terminated effective immediately. You will see that in Level 4. You'll see that in Level 4.

levels.name: Chloe, 25, Junior Analyst
levels.story: The 8 levels of job hunting after a master degree. Level 4. Level 4: 3.100 dollars a month, living with three roommates, and still unable to afford dental care. I sat in the sterile plastic chair of the corporate lobby, nervously adjusting my blazer while my forehead display glowed with my entry-level salary. My skin is a smooth, bright orange peel with tiny pores, wearing a budget polyester skirt suit and scuffed black heels. With a Master degree in data science, I expected more than a cubicle next to the copier machine. My cheeks burned hot crimson as I spotted a tiny gold coin tucked inside the groove of the elevator track. I crunched numbers all weekend for your department while you took credit for my models. People with your numbers do not belong on the executive floor, darling. My breath hitched in my throat as my hands began to tremble uncontrollably. You will never get promoted past assistant. You will see that in Level 5. You'll see that in Level 5.

levels.name: Julian, 31, Project Manager
levels.story: The 8 levels of job hunting after a master degree. Level 5. Level 5: 5.400 dollars a month, driving a leased sedan, and still drowning in student loan payments. I stood in the glass-walled conference room, pointing at the quarterly growth charts while my forehead flashed my middle-management salary. My skin is a bumpy, forest-green avocado person with a smooth light-green center tint, wearing a tailored slim-fit suit and designer glasses. You think your little Master in project management makes you an expert, but you do not know how the real world operates. My teeth clicked together angrily as I noticed a tiny gold coin resting on the edge of the projector stand. I doubled your department output last quarter, and you denied my promotion request. Middle-management drones like you are easily replaced by software, my friend. My pulse raced like a drumbeat as the air in the room turned ice-cold. You have reached your absolute ceiling in this company. You will see that in Level 6. You'll see that in Level 6.

levels.name: Victoria, 38, Department Director
levels.story: The 8 levels of job hunting after a master degree. Level 6. Level 6: 9.800 dollars a month, a penthouse apartment, and total control over sixty subordinates. I sat in my leather executive chair, reviewing the annual hiring budgets while my glowing forehead display showed my upper-management salary. My skin is a crisp, brilliant red pomegranate shell with tiny jewel-like seeds visible around my temples, wearing a designer crimson sheath dress and pearl earrings. With a Master in corporate law, I deserve a director seat instead of fetching your morning tea. My patience snapped instantly as I spotted a tiny gold coin gleaming inside my crystal pen holder. I gave you a platform when no one else would look at your zero-dollar forehead. You climbed up by stepping on everyone else, and your time at the top is almost over. My chest tightened with sudden anxiety as the office temperature seemed to drop. Your position is being eliminated tomorrow morning. You will see that in Level 7. You'll see that in Level 7.

levels.name: Sophia, 52, Founder & CEO
levels.story: The 8 levels of job hunting after a master degree. Level 8. Level 8: Unlimited wealth, the entire corporation in my hands, and the secret knowledge of every single number in this city. I sat at the head of the grand marble table, looking at the glowing forehead displays of all eight produce people standing together in my boardroom. My skin is a smooth, golden-yellow starfruit surface with crisp geometric ridges, wearing a minimalist white silk jumpsuit and a diamond pendant. We all thought the number on our forehead defined our worth, but the system was rigged from the very beginning. A heavy silence fell across the room as the digital displays across all eight foreheads began to flicker and shift simultaneously. I smiled softly, leaning back into my leather chair while watching their stunned expressions. Every single struggle, every rejection letter, and every bitter confrontation was just a test to see who would survive the climb. The number on your forehead is not your value, it is simply your current coordinates in the game. Which topic should we explore in the next series? The End.
